sections.title: Overview
blocks: **Discoid lupus erythematosus** is the most common form of **chronic cutaneous lupus**. Scarring inflammatory plaques favour head and neck; scalp disease causes **scarring alopecia**. Most patients have skin-limited disease, but a minority evolve toward systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Module 4 Formative Quiz-1 answer was DLE (vs alopecia areata, LPP, tinea capitis, trichotillomania).

ul: Autoimmune interface dermatitis with follicular involvement.

Risk factors emphasised in teaching: **darker skin phototypes** have higher rates of DLE and more disfiguring dyspigmentation/scarring; smoking associated with DLE activity/treatment resistance; female predominance overall (quiz noted male sex is *not* the higher-risk factor).

ddx.name: Alopecia areata
ddx.f: Non-scarring; exclamation hairs; no discoid scale plaques

ddx.name: Lichen planopilaris
ddx.f: Scarring; perifollicular scale; less classic facial discoid plaques

ddx.name: Trichotillomania
ddx.f: Bizarre geometric; hairs of different lengths

ul: Potent/very potent TCS or intralesional steroid (often derm); topical calcineurin inhibitors on face sometimes.
Early derm referral for scalp/face to minimise irreversible scarring.
Screen for SLE symptoms (arthritis, serositis, renal, photosensitivity beyond skin, cytopenias).

refer.t: Joint pain, mouth ulcers, fatigue, chest pain or Raynaud’s: screen for **SLE** (ANA, FBC, urine dipstick) and refer.
Scalp DLE with hair loss: **urgent** dermatology (scarring alopecia).
Hydroxychloroquine: baseline and annual eye screening after 5 years (RCOphth).

pearls: Emphasise scarring risk — early treatment matters.
Camouflage / psychological support for visible disease.
Check BNF interactions if hydroxychloroquine co-prescribed later (retinopathy monitoring is specialty).
